pr_title: Special case the posix locale in WildcardPattern
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary

Fix #10177
Special case the posix locale in WildcardPattern.
When `WildcardOptions.IgnoreCase` is specified and the current culture is `en-us-POSIX`, we use `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase` instead of `StringComparison.CurrentCultureIgnoreCase`, because the Posix culture compares in case-sensitive manner only.

export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8

review_comments:
Should we add a test case?

We have one for.. hashtable.

Looking how we use WildcardPattern.IsMatch() I am sure that in most of cases we can definitely replace `StringComparison.CurrentCultureIgnoreCase` with `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase`. One place where we should be careful is HelpSystem but where we could use Regex directly.

I'm not sure about it. Quoted from doc about [StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.stringcomparer.ordinalignorecase?view=netframework-4.8#remarks):
>The StringComparer returned by the OrdinalIgnoreCase property treats the characters in the strings to compare as if they were converted to uppercase **using the conventions of the invariant culture**, and then performs a simple byte comparison that is independent of language.

So when using `OrdinalIgnoreCase`, it will actually use `invariant culture` to convert characters to upper case. This makes me nervous about using `OrdinalIgnoreCase` in general for wildcard matching.
To avoid potential regression, I prefer to special case the POSIX-locale and use `OrdinalIgnoreCase` only for that culture.

Sorry, my comment was out of the context. I meant that we do culture-sensitive comparisons while we should be culture-insensitive (ordinal) in most of cases where WildcardPattern is used.

As for your fix  it is LGTM.
